full_details: Twenty shillings went on her table and she counted them twice. The firing sixpence ended until Michaelmas. You said the year had changed and the room had not improved, and she called constancy one of its virtues and wrote the receipt in her husband's law-hand. She will keep the chamber. Upstairs you ruled a line, headed the page 1595, and wrote a horn of her ink at twopence and a quire at fivepence under the twenty shillings. You counted the coffer at twenty-seven pounds and two shillings. The sevenpence is on the page and does not change that sum. The sixty shillings of canvas were still inside the count. The long page stayed on the board. You took the canvas and five pounds more into the belt, for the road and your father's shops, and you locked nineteen pounds and two shillings behind both locks. Nothing in the talk was about a name or a coat. In the afternoon she gave you small beer and her blessing on the road. At four you were at St Helen's for evening prayer, and you did not take the receipt into the pew. The bay was still not taken.
one_sentence: You paid the quarter before noon, wrote 1595 over a ruled line, and locked nineteen pounds two shillings under both locks.
title: Paid the quarter and headed the page 1595
